adverse_media.status: FCA enquiries made; investigation closed about a year later
adverse_media.summary: A former employee complained to the FCA in 2016 about compliance weaknesses and the conduct of CEO Nikolay Storonsky; the FCA made enquiries and told the whistleblower its investigation was 'coming to a close' a year later
BBC/Wired exposé on Revolut's high-pressure culture and compliance frictions; former employee said 'the CEO refused to listen to the compliance team'

adverse_media.status: fines imposed; remediation reported by 30 Jun 2022
adverse_media.summary: Bank of Lithuania sanctioned Revolut group companies: €50,000 fine on Revolut Bank UAB and €150,000 on Revolut Payments UAB for AML/CFT breaches (onboarding risk factors, senior-management approval for higher-risk clients and PEPs not always ensured)

FCA warned the public about a scam impersonating Revolut Ltd (fake 'Al-pha Bank' contacts) — fraud against the firm's customers, not misconduct by Revolut
3,015 new Financial Ombudsman Service complaints about Revolut Ltd in Jan–Jun 2025, 33% upheld (31% median), of which 3,012 about banking and credit
Revolut's Australian subsidiary was fined A$187,800 (~$123,000) for breaching AML rules by submitting late reports

FT reported Revolut did not inform UK regulators before a Companies House filing listing CEO Storonsky as UAE-resident, prompting questions from the FCA, Bank of England and Treasury during the banking-licence process; filing later amended

Italy's competition authority fined Revolut group companies more than €11.5m ($13.25m) for alleged unfair commercial practices — misleading statements on investment services and aggressive/deceptive management of banking services; Revolut 'strongly disagrees' and is appealing

adverse_media.status: resolved — 2021 accounts signed off in early March 2023 after accounting-system overhaul
adverse_media.summary: Auditor BDO LLP flagged concerns over the 'completeness and occurrence' of £477m ($576m) of revenues in Revolut's 2021 accounts, delaying sign-off for months; Revolut said the revenue figure 'was not in question' and concerns were remedied

adverse_media.status: subsequently reconciled; full banking licence granted 11 Mar 2026
adverse_media.summary: In 2023 auditors issued a qualified opinion on Revolut's accounts, saying it was unable to verify a portion of revenues; the Bank of England that year told the Treasury it planned to reject the banking application

adverse_media.status: settled — Revolut signed a settlement and took remediation steps; company says no confirmed money-laundering instances
adverse_media.summary: Bank of Lithuania fined Revolut €3.5m ($3.83m) — the largest fine it has ever issued — for AML prevention failures: inspection found violations and shortcomings in monitoring of business relationships and operations, with suspicious transactions not always properly identified

output.risk_rationale: MEDIUM. Revolut Ltd is a verified, active private limited company (Companies House 08804411, incorporated 6 Dec 2013, 30 South Colonnade, London) with an issued, fully-corroborated LEI (213800MQORWPL582SW82), FCA authorisation (FRN 900562) and, since 11 March 2026, a full UK banking licence. No sanctions match exists for the company, its parent (Revolut Group Holdings Ltd, 75–100% owner since 2022) or its directors on OFAC SDN, UK OFSI or the EU consolidated list; the only name match — Ukraine NSDC-sanctioned Nikolay Storonsky (b. 1963, CEO of state-owned Gazprom Promgaz) — is a different party believed to be the CEO's father, which leaves a PEP-adjacent family/sanctions-proximity flag on the founder-CEO (who renounced his Russian citizenship in 2022 and is not himself a PEP). The rating is lifted above low by the adverse-media record: the Bank of Lithuania's €3.5m AML fine (April 2025, the largest it has ever issued), earlier Lithuanian AML fines on group entities (2022), Austrac A$187,800 (2025), Italy's €11.5m consumer-protection fine (April 2026, under appeal), auditor BDO's concerns over £477m of 2021 revenue (resolved March 2023) and the December 2025 UAE-residency filing affair, plus an overdue confirmation statement. Balanced against a clean UK-entity regulatory record (no FCA actions), full licence grant in March 2026 and remediation across the fines, the composite residual risk is medium.
